name: Białowieża Forest
description: Białowieża Forest is one of the last big remnants of the primeval woodland that once blanketed the European Plain, straddling the Polish–Belarusian border about 62 km southeast of Białystok. Its mix of conifers and broadleaved trees covers nearly 142,000 hectares. It shelters the world's largest population of European bison, Europe's heaviest land animal, and hikers and cyclists can cross the border here on foot or by bike.
